title: Competitive playbook for quantized model adoption in enterprise customers
creator: Lena Park
description: Background: As open models proliferate, enterprise buyers often prefer quantized model variants (4-bit/8-bit) to reduce cost and enable on-prem/private deployment, but quantization introduces non-linear quality regressions and hardware affinity constraints. Goal: produce a reproducible playbook that lets Redwood sales, solutions, and product teams evaluate and communicate tradeoffs for quantized model adoption in regulated enterprises. Scope: competitive signal map, decision heuristics, field interview guide, measurable POC plan (latency/cost/quality), and a procurement trigger rubric that ties to Dedicated/Private offerings. Out-of-scope: deep model research into quantization algorithms (this ticket focuses on buyer-facing decision framework and operational instrumentation).
acceptance_criteria: Competitive signal map covering at least 6 major open-model families and 3 commercial providers with quantized variant availability

Decision heuristic matrix that maps workload archetypes (short-chat, summarization, embedding search, RAG) to recommended config (precision, batching, KV cache policy, fallback model) and explicit tradeoffs
Field interview guide + 6 validated enterprise interviews (notes imported to Drive) with procurement and ML platform leads
POC checklist and telemetry spec for evaluating quality regressions (token-level diffs, hallucination rates, latency percentiles, cost per 1k tokens)
Procurement trigger rubric that outputs recommended pathway (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) and contractual language snippets for SRE/Legal
Dashboard prototype wireframe in Confluence linking model-variant signals to sales enablement artefacts
deliverables: Demo notebook for rapid quantized-vs-fp comparison (GitHub PR: rw/benchmarks#482)
tasks: 01. Assemble competitor matrix (data sources: release notes, model hubs, vendor pages)
02. Define workload archetypes and quality signals we will measure
03. Draft decision heuristic matrix and circulate to SRE and Solutions Eng for feedback
04. Run 3 small synthetic POCs (search, summarization, chat) with candidate quantized variants
05. Instrument telemetry and produce baseline dashboards
06. Conduct 6 enterprise interviews (sales + SE to coordinate), summarize findings
07. Draft procurement rubric and legal snippets; review with Legal
08. Finalize playbook and publish Confluence + sales one-pager
